root_cause.text: The freemap adjustment logic in `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()` failed to update all freemap entries when the leaf entry array expanded, allowing freemap entries to claim space that overlapped with the growing entries array, causing memory corruption and assertion failures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the original code only adjusted freemap entries where `ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp` (the old end of the entries array), but this missed cases where freemap entries had bases between the old and new end positions. The CVE description demonstrates this: when the entries array grew from 448 to 456 bytes, freemap[1] with base=388 was never updated, creating an overlap where "the entries array and the free space claim the same space." The fix adds a second condition `ichdr->freemap[i].base < new_end` to catch and adjust all freemap entries that collide with the expanded entries array, not just those at the exact old boundary.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix freemap adjustment logic to correctly handle overlapping freemap entries when expanding the leaf entry array, not just those starting at the exact old boundary.
intent_record.what: Refactored the freemap adjustment logic in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work by introducing new_end and old_end variables, replacing a single conditional check with two separate conditions to handle different freemap overlap scenarios, and updating the diff calculation to use the computed diff value instead of a hardcoded sizeof expression.
intent_record.how: The change improves handling of freemap entries when adding a new leaf entry. Previously, only freemap entries starting exactly at the old end position were adjusted. Now it also handles freemap entries that overlap with the newly claimed space by the expanded leaf entry array, adjusting their base and size more accurately based on the actual overlap region rather than a fixed size.

It does not implement any actual logic fixes to address the freemap adjustment issue or prevent the overlap between freemap entries and the expanding leaf entry array. Variable declarations alone do not fix the vulnerability; the actual freemap update logic changes would be needed in subsequent groups.

The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the freemap adjustment logic to handle overlapping freemap entries when the leaf entry array expands. The vulnerability occurred because not all freemap entries were updated when the array expanded, causing overlaps. This fix corrects that exact issue by ensuring overlapping entries (not just those at the exact boundary) are properly adjusted.

candidates.rationale: This condition only adjusts freemap entries that start exactly at the old boundary (tmp). It fails to handle freemap entries that overlap with the expanding entry array but don't start at the exact boundary, allowing those entries to claim space that now overlaps with the grown entries array.

This adjustment only applies when the freemap base equals tmp exactly. Overlapping freemap entries that don't meet this condition are not adjusted, leaving them to claim corrupted/overlapping space as the entry array expands.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is too restrictive and only adjusts freemap entries whose base equals exactly tmp (the old boundary). It fails to handle freemap entries that overlap with the expanding entry array but start before tmp, allowing those overlapping entries to retain stale base values that claim space now occupied by the grown entries array, causing memory corruption.

This adjustment only executes when the preceding condition (base == tmp) is true, meaning overlapping freemap entries that don't start at the exact boundary are never adjusted. These unadjusted entries continue to claim space that now overlaps with the expanded entry array, directly causing the memory corruption vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
xfs: add CRCs to attr leaf blocks

Signed-off-by: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Ben Myers <bpm@sgi.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in lines 1422-1427. The freemap adjustment logic only updates freemap entries where `ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp` (line 1423). However, when the entry array expands due to the memmove at line 1341 and ichdr->count increment at line 1345, the freemap entries need to be adjusted to account for the growing entries array. The current logic only adjusts the freemap entry whose base exactly matches the calculated tmp value, but it fails to adjust all freemap entries that should be shifted. This allows freemap entries to claim space that overlaps with the growing entries array. The fix would require adjusting all freemap entries whose base falls within the range affected by the entry array expansion, not just the one matching the exact tmp value. The code lacks the comprehensive freemap update logic needed to prevent memory corruption when the entries array grows.

xfs: add CRCs to attr leaf blocks

Signed-off-by: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Ben Myers <bpm@sgi.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in lines 1422-1427. The freemap adjustment logic only updates freemap entries where `ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp` (line 1423). However, when the entry array expands at line 1341 (memmove operation), the entry array grows by `sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t)`. The loop at lines 1422-1427 only adjusts freemap entries that have their base exactly equal to `tmp` (the new boundary after entry array expansion). This is insufficient because: (1) it only updates ONE freemap entry that matches the exact condition, and (2) it fails to account for all freemap entries that may have their space overlapped by the growing entry array. The vulnerability allows freemap entries to claim space that overlaps with the expanded entries array, causing memory corruption. The fix would require updating ALL freemap entries whose base falls within the range affected by the entry array expansion, not just the one matching the exact boundary condition.
